verdict.rationale: Rive's docs describe Components as reusable artboards whose customized instances stay linked to the source: changes to the source component are reflected across all of its instances. That covers reuse, per-instance customization and linkage. Nothing in the evidence documents variants, and 'customized instances' is the only description of how overrides work. missing for 10: documented component variants, detail on per-instance override behavior and how overrides survive source changes, independent or hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As a designer, I can build reusable components with variants and per-instance overrides that stay linked to their source

citations.quote: Components are reusable artboards. Create a component once, then use customized instances of it throughout your Rive file.
Changes made to the source component are reflected across all of its instances.
Create vector graphics, responsive layouts, and reusable components
